blocks.text: A maintenance team removes the same inspection cover on a conveyor every week. After a year the aluminium threads are stripped, and the bolts that held fine on day one now fall out under vibration. Fastener choice decided both failures.

blocks.markdown: A fastener choice answers three questions: **how often** will the joint be taken apart, **what material** holds the thread, and **what loads and vibration** act on it. Common standard fasteners are the hexagon-head bolt (used with a nut), the screw (threaded into a tapped hole), the **socket head cap screw (SHCS)**, and the stud. Washers spread load and protect the surface; nuts complete a bolted joint.

rows: Fair in steel, poor in soft metal
blocks.caption: Choosing a fastener for a joint that must be opened often

blocks.title: Repeated disassembly
blocks.text: Put the wearing thread on something replaceable: a nut, a stud or a steel thread insert. Do not repeatedly thread a screw into soft aluminium or plastic.

blocks.markdown: **Clearance and counterbore for a socket head cap screw.** The screw passes through a **clearance hole** slightly larger than its nominal diameter $d$. Two typical ISO-style series are *fine* and *medium*; typical medium values are M6: 6.6 mm, M8: 9 mm, M10: 11 mm, M12: 13.5 mm. The cylindrical head, of diameter about $1.5d$ and height about $d$ (typical for an SHCS), can be sunk in a **counterbore** so it sits flush or below the surface. The counterbore diameter must exceed the head diameter by a margin for a socket key and clearance, and its depth must exceed the head height.

blocks.caption: Typical SHCS hole data (representative values; check the manufacturer or standard table)

blocks.title: Flush-mounting an M10 screw
blocks.prompt: An M10 SHCS (head diameter 16 mm, head height 10 mm) is to sit 1 mm below the surface of a 25 mm plate. Specify clearance hole, counterbore diameter and depth, and the plate thickness left under the head.

steps.text: Use the typical medium clearance hole for M10.
Counterbore diameter from the table, 18 mm, which exceeds the 16 mm head by 1 mm per side.
Depth: head height plus the 1 mm recess.

blocks.answer: 11 mm clearance hole, 18 mm counterbore 11 mm deep, leaving 14 mm of plate.

blocks.title: Choosing the screw length
blocks.prompt: An M8 SHCS clamps a plate 18 mm thick, with a counterbore 8.5 mm deep, to an aluminium base. Required thread engagement in the base is 1.5 d. What is the minimum screw length (under the head)?

steps.text: Material under the head: plate thickness minus counterbore depth.

blocks.answer: At least 21.5 mm, so choose the next standard length, 25 mm.

blocks.markdown: **Locking against vibration.** Vibration can cause a preloaded joint to lose preload and loosen. A plain washer or plain nut does not prevent this. Common remedies: a **prevailing-torque (nylon-insert) nut** (typical limit about 120 degrees C for the nylon), an **all-metal prevailing-torque nut** for high temperature, a **thread-locking adhesive** applied to the thread, a **serrated flange** fastener, **wire or split-pin locking** for safety-critical joints, and a **double nut**. Spring washers give little reliable protection.

blocks.title: Plain washers do not lock
blocks.text: A plain flat washer spreads load; it does not stop a nut turning. Spring washers are often over-trusted.

points: For repeated disassembly put the thread in a replaceable component: a nut, stud or insert.
An SHCS needs a clearance hole and, if flush, a counterbore larger than the head and deeper than the head height.
Vibration needs a real locking method: prevailing-torque nut, adhesive, wire or serrated flange.

questions.stem: A moulded plastic lid is removed every month for cleaning. Which fastening is the best choice?

options.text: Screws cut directly into the plastic
Screws into metal thread inserts fitted in the plastic

questions.correctOptionText: Screws into metal thread inserts fitted in the plastic
questions.explanation: A metal insert carries the wearing thread, so the plastic is not damaged by repeated screwing. Threads cut in soft material strip; rivets cannot be removed.

questions.stem: A bolt on a vibrating machine loosens despite a plain washer. Which change best prevents it?
questions.explanation: A prevailing-torque nut resists rotation by friction independent of preload. A plain washer cannot lock the nut.

questions.stem: An M12 socket head cap screw has a head height equal to its nominal diameter. It is to sit 1.0 mm below the surface in a counterbore. What counterbore depth is needed, in mm?
questions.explanation: Depth is head height plus recess: 12 + 1.0 = 13 mm. The counterbore must be at least this deep.

questions.stem: An M8 SHCS clamps a 22 mm plate with an 8.5 mm deep counterbore into a steel base. The thread engagement required is 1.0 d, with d = 8 mm. Calculate the minimum screw length under the head in mm.
questions.explanation: Material under the head is 22 - 8.5 = 13.5 mm and engagement is 8 mm, giving 21.5 mm. The next standard length, 25 mm, would be chosen.

questions.stem: Using the typical medium clearance series, what clearance hole diameter is used for an M10 screw?
questions.explanation: The typical medium clearance for M10 is 11 mm, slightly larger than 10 mm to allow for hole position error. 13.5 mm is for M12 and 9 mm for M8.

questions.stem: A joint on an engine exhaust runs at about 300 degrees C and vibrates. Which locking method is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Nylon degrades at the temperature, so an all-metal locknut is needed. Plain and spring washers do not lock reliably.

questions.stem: A cover is opened weekly, is made of magnesium alloy, and must resist vibration. Which choice satisfies both needs?

options.text: Screws tapped directly into magnesium with a spring washer
Steel inserts with screws and a locking adhesive of medium strength

questions.correctOptionText: Steel inserts with screws and a locking adhesive of medium strength

distractorRationale.a: Wears and spring washers are weak.

questions.explanation: The steel insert protects the soft thread under repeated opening, and a medium-strength removable adhesive resists vibration. The others fail one of the two requirements.

questions.stem: Specify the holes needed to mount an M8 socket head cap screw flush with a 20 mm plate surface. State clearance diameter, counterbore diameter and minimum depth, using the typical values stated in the lesson.
markingGuide: Counterbore 15 mm, larger than the 13 mm head
Depth at least the head height 8 mm, plus a recess
Plate under the counterbore remains for support
questions.explanation: The answer must give hole diameters above the screw and head diameters and a depth above the head height. Each point in the marking guide earns credit, so state every point explicitly and give its reason.

questions.stem: A joint on a pump skid is removed monthly and the skid vibrates. Recommend a fastening arrangement and justify it, covering thread location and locking.
markingGuide: Through bolt with nut or stud and nut, so the nut thread wears
Or steel insert in soft base
Prevailing-torque nut or thread-locking adhesive for vibration
Plain washer under the nut to protect the surface
questions.explanation: A strong answer places the wearing thread on a replaceable part and gives a real locking mechanism. Each point in the marking guide earns credit, so state every point explicitly and give its reason.

questions.stem: A plain flat washer alone prevents a nut from loosening under vibration.
questions.explanation: A plain washer only spreads load. Loosening is resisted by prevailing torque, adhesives or positive locking.
